Final for Publication

NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
3100-08 WEST LAKE STREET, CHICAGO

The subject property is currently a vacant parcel. The Applicant intends to redevelop this lot with
anew one-story commercial building and establish a Contractor/Construction Storage Yard (with
indoor and outdoor storage). A zoning change is needed to allow such proposed use at the
property and to receive any relief necessary for the proposed redevelopment. _

Project Zoning Change from an M1-3 Limited Manufacturing/Business Park

Description: District to an M2-3 Light Industry District

Use: Commercial Building (contractor / construction storage yard with
indoor and outdoor storage)

Lot Area: 104.05’ x 106’ = 10,463 SF (recorded measurements)

Floor Area Ratio: | 0.5

Floor Area: 4,500 SF (see plans attached)

Density: N/A

Off- Street Parking: | Parking spaces: 4 (see adjustment request below)

Setbacks: Front: 3’-3”
Side: 3’-0” on the west side and 7’ on the east side
Rear: 3’-6” (see variation request below)

Building Height: | 24’ per the attached plans


Final for Publication

1 Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section t7-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) With this Type 1 Rezoning, if needed, the Applicant also seeks relief for Administrative
Adjustment under section 17-13-1003-EE, from the parking requirements of Section 17-
10-0207-O (which states that the parking requirements for the proposed use is 1.66 spaces
per 1,000 square feet of improvements) to decrease the on-site parking requirements from
8 parking spaces required to 4 parking spaces, as proposed, as authorized by Section 17-
10-0102-B Transit-Served Locations. The subject property is a Transit Served Location as
it is situated within 600 feet from the Green Line CTA Station at Kedzie and Lake.

(B) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under section 17-13-1101-B, from rear
setback requirements of Section 17-5-0405-B Rear Setbacks, which states that no rear
setback is required in M districts, except when the rear property line of an M-zoned site
abuts the side property line or rear property line of a lot in an R district or is separated
from an R district rear property line by an alley, the minimum rear setback on the M-
zoned property is 30 feet. To mitigate site planning hardships on this substandard depth
lot, the Applicant requests a reduction in the required rear setback from 30 feet required to
3 feet 6 inches proposed.

{C) The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for the
proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

1, Practical Difficulties and Hardship:
Strict application of the requirements of this Zoning Ordinance would impose undue
practical difficulties and hardship on the subject property. Specifically, the lot has a depth
of only 106 feet, which is approximately 19 feet less than the standard lot depth within the
City, and as defined in the Ordinance. This substandard condition materially limits the
ability to reasonably develop the property in full compliance with the Ordinance.
2. Consistency with the Purpose and Intent of the Ordinance
The requested variations are consistent with the purpose and intent of the Zoning
Ordinance. The proposed redevelopment is compatible with the established development
pattern on the subject block, which is characterized by improved properties that do not
uniformly conform to current setback requirements. Accordingly, granting the requested
relief will maintain continuity with the existing built environment and advance the
Ordinance’s broader planning objectives.
3. Evidence of Practical Difficulties and Particular Hardship
- The property cannot be reasonably developed or yield a viable economic retum if
restricted to strict compliance with the Ordinance due to its deficient lot depth. The
proposed redevelopment represents a reasonable and appropriate use of the property
under these site planning constraints.

Final for Publication

- The hardship arises from unique physical characteristics of the property, including its
substandard depth and comer configuration. The lot abuts three public rights-of-way, a
condition not generally applicable to similarly situated properties. The requested relief
is necessary to accommodate functional site planning elements, including adequate
parking and screening for indoor and outdoor storage, while responding to these
constraints. The corner location also ensures sufficient access to light and air for the
proposed development and will not negatively impact adjacent properties,

- Approval of the requested variations and administrative adjustment will not alter the
essential character of the neighborhood. The surrounding area includes numerous

Properties that do not strictly comply with current bulk, setback, and parking
requirements. As such, the proposed development will be consistent with the
prevailing character and scale of the neighborhood.
